'''Gregor William Yeates''', publishing as '''GW Yeates''' (19 May 1944&nbsp;– 6 August 2012),<ref name="obit">Death Notice, page 23, [[Manawatu Standard]], 8 August 2012</ref><ref name="obit2">{{cite journal |last1=Wardle |first1=David A. |last2=Ross |first2=Craig |date=2013 |title=Gregor William Yeates, 19 May 1944–6 August 2012 |url=http://newzealandecology.org/nzje/3059 |journal=[[New Zealand Journal of Ecology]] |volume=37 |issue=1 |pages=156–158}}</ref> was a New Zealand soil zoologist and ecologist. He was "considered the world's leading authority in soil nematode ecology, a subject of economic and ecological importance."<ref name="fellow"/>

==Scientific career and contributions==
As a student Yeates counted [[Adélie penguin]]s at [[Cape Royds]] in 1964–65 and 1965–66.<ref>Yeates, G. W. 1968: Studies on the Adelie Penguin at Cape Royds 1964–65 and 1965–66. New Zealand Journal of Marine and Freshwater Research 2: 472–496.</ref> His PhD (under [[Wally Clark (zoologist)|Wally Clark]])<ref>{{cite web |date=2012 |title=Newsletter, Biological Sciences – University of Canterbury – New Zealand |url= https://www.canterbury.ac.nz/science/schools/biological-sciences/about-the-school/newsletters/2012-Biological-Sciences-Newsletters.pdf |accessdate=17 May 2022}}</ref> was on [[nematode]]s of dune sands, and was completed in 1968 at the [[University of Canterbury]].<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Yeates |first=G. |year=1968 |type=Doctoral thesis |title=Studies on nematodes of dune sands |publisher=UC Research Repository, University of Canterbury |hdl=10092/4945 |doi=10.26021/8148 |url=https://ir.canterbury.ac.nz/handle/10092/4945}}</ref> His DSc was also at the University of Canterbury.<ref>{{cite thesis | last = Yeates | first = Gregor William | title = Studies on soil nematode populations | place = [[Christchurch]] | publisher = [[University of Canterbury]] | type = DSc | year = 1985}}</ref> Yeates's early work on nematodes in sand dunes represented some of the first detailed work on nematodes in non-agricultural settings, and 'representing some of the most detailed assessments of nematode communities ever conducted in natural environments.'<ref name="Pedobiologia">{{cite journal|title=Resolution of respect for Gregor William Yeates, 1944–2012|first1=David A. |last1=Wardle|first2=Craig|last2=Ross |first3=Brian|last3=Boag|first4=David C.|last4=Coleman|date=10 November 2012 |journal=Pedobiologia |volume=55 |issue=6 |pages=283–284 |doi=10.1016/j.pedobi.2012.10.002|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Yeates spent most of his working life at [[Soil Bureau]], a division of [[Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (New Zealand)|DSIR]], which became [[Landcare Research]].<ref name="bio">{{cite web |url=http://plpnemweb.ucdavis.edu/nemaplex/General/Biographies/GYeates.htm |title=Gregor Yeates |publisher=Plpnemweb.ucdavis.edu |date=5 August 2012 |accessdate=10 August 2012 |archive-date=5 March 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120305013819/http://plpnemweb.ucdavis.edu/nemaplex/General/Biographies/GYeates.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> He published over 200 papers and described over 100 species in genera including [[Wikispecies:Longidorus|Longidorus]], [[Wikispecies:Xiphinema|Xiphinema]], [[Hemicycliophora]], [[Wikispecies:Trischistoma|Trischistoma]] and [[Dorylaimida]]. [[Holotype]]s of his are the earliest in the [[National Nematode Collection of New Zealand]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.landcareresearch.co.nz/resources/collections/nncnz |title=National Nematode Collection of New Zealand (NNCNZ) |publisher=Landcare Research |date=31 May 2010 |accessdate=10 August 2012 |archive-date=7 February 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130207132857/http://www.landcareresearch.co.nz/resources/collections/nncnz |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was awarded a Nuffield Foundation Commonwealth Travelling Fellowship to study at Rothamsted in 1977–1978.<ref name="Pedobiologia"/> He conducted long-term work on [[CO2|CO<sub>2</sub>]] enrichment in pasture.<ref name="Pedobiologia"/> He studied the [[New Zealand flatworm]] ''[[Arthurdendyus triangulatus]]'' in its native environment,<ref name="Pedobiologia"/> supporting work in the United Kingdom where it became established as an invasive pest.

==Family and civic life==
Yeates was the son of [[Massey University]] founding staff member [[John Stuart Yeates]]. He and wife Judy lived in [[Upper Hutt]] and [[Palmerston North]], with two children. He was elected to the [[Rimutaka ward]] of the [[Upper Hutt City Council]] (1973–1977) and the [[Hutt Valley Drainage Board]] (1973–1977). He was later involved with [[Te Manawa, Palmerston North|Te Manawa]] in [[Palmerston North]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.register.charities.govt.nz/CharitiesRegister/ViewCharity?accountId=dfd2515a-2e93-dc11-8026-0015c5f3da29|title=Charities Register|accessdate=7 September 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.register.charities.govt.nz/CharitiesRegister/ViewCharity?accountId=8cde7d2c-f41e-dd11-99cd-0015c5f3da29|title=Charities Register|accessdate=7 September 2016}}</ref><ref name='leader'>Obitrary. [[Upper Hutt]] Leader. 15 August 2012</ref> and the [[Royal Society of New Zealand]] at both a local<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.register.charities.govt.nz/CharitiesRegister/ViewCharity?accountId=1edee514-9958-df11-b1a3-0015c5f3da29|title=Charities Register|accessdate=7 September 2016}}</ref> and a national level.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.register.charities.govt.nz/CharitiesRegister/ViewCharity?accountId=56035877-c08e-df11-871d-00155d741101|title=Charities Register|accessdate=7 September 2016}}</ref><ref>[http://www.parliament.nz/mi-NZ/PB/SC/Documents/Evidence/6/4/2/49SCES_EVI_00DBHOH_BILL10335_1_A144660-Dr-G-W-Yeates-and-Royal-Society.htm New Zealand Parliament – Dr G W Yeates and Royal Society of New Zealand Manawatu Branch<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

* Fellow of the [[New Zealand Society of Soil Science]] (1995)<ref name="bio"/>
* Fellow of the [[Society of Nematologists]] (2007)<ref name="bio"/>
* Editorial Board of [[Journal of Nematology]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.journal-of-nematology-style-guide.org/ed-board.html |title=The JOURNAL of NEMATOLOGY &#124; Style Guide |publisher=Journal-of-nematology-style-guide.org |date=31 December 2011 |accessdate=10 August 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120930014751/http://www.journal-of-nematology-style-guide.org/ed-board.html |archivedate=30 September 2012 |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

* Officeholder in the [[Royal Society of New Zealand]] Wellington Branch from 1981, including 1987–88<ref name="rsnzobit">{{cite web|url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/organisation/academy/fellowship/obituaries/gregor-yeates/|title=Gregor William Yeates|accessdate=7 September 2016}}</ref>
* [[Upper Hutt City]] Councillor and [[Hutt Valley]] Drainage Board member from 1973 to 1977<ref name="rsnzobit"/>
*  Council of the New Zealand Rhododendron Association 1997–2000<ref name="rsnzobit"/>
* Heritage Park Rhododendron Charitable Trust Trustee<ref name="rsnzobit"/>
* President of the New Zealand Society of Parasitology 1990–1991<ref name="rsnzobit"/>
